next_state_election.name: General Election
next_state_election.source_name: Pennsylvania Department of State — Upcoming Elections

glance_notes.source_name: Pennsylvania Department of State — Upcoming Elections
glance_notes.text: 2026 General Election Registration Deadline: Pennsylvania's voter registration deadline for the November 3, 2026 General Election is October 19. Pennsylvania requires registration at least 15 days before an election.

glance_notes.source_name: Pennsylvania Department of State — On-Demand Mail Ballot Voting
glance_notes.text: No Traditional Early Voting: Pennsylvania does not operate traditional early-voting polling places. Once ballots are available, a registered voter may apply for, receive, complete and return a mail-in or absentee ballot during one visit to a county election office or another officially designated location.

glance_notes.source_name: Pennsylvania Department of State — Mail-in and Absentee Ballot
glance_notes.text: No-Excuse Mail Voting: Any registered Pennsylvania voter may apply for a no-excuse mail-in ballot. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, the county election office must receive the application by 5:00 p.m. October 27 and must receive the completed civilian mail ballot by 8:00 p.m. November 3.

register.label: Register to Vote
register.content: Eligible Pennsylvania residents may register online, by mail, in person at a county voter registration office or through authorized government agencies including PennDOT Photo License and Driver's License Centers. To register, a person must be a U.S. citizen for at least one month before the election, have been a resident of Pennsylvania and the election district for at least 30 days before the election, and be at least 18 years old on or before Election Day. Pennsylvania requires registration at least 15 days before an election.
register.glance_value: Online, mail, county office or authorized agencies
register.source_name: Pennsylvania Department of State — Voter Registration
register.internal_note: Pennsylvania's eligibility requirements are unusually specific: citizenship for at least one month before the election and residence in Pennsylvania and the election district for at least 30 days. Registration closes 15 days before an election. Pennsylvania does not provide general same-day registration.

check_registration.label: Check Voter Registration
check_registration.content: Use Pennsylvania's official voter registration status system to confirm that you are registered and that your voter information is current. Voters should check their record after moving or changing their name. County election officials can resolve questions about a registration record.
check_registration.source_name: Pennsylvania Department of State — Voter Registration Status
check_registration.internal_note: The Department of State directly provides the statewide registration-status lookup and directs voters to county election officials for voter-specific questions.

deadlines.label: Registration Deadlines
deadlines.content: Pennsylvania requires voter registration at least 15 days before an election. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, the registration deadline is Monday, October 19. A registration application must be received by the appropriate voter registration office by the deadline. Pennsylvania does not provide general same-day registration during the period before Election Day or at the polls.
deadlines.source_name: Pennsylvania Department of State — Upcoming Elections
deadlines.internal_note: The official 2026 Pennsylvania election calendar directly establishes October 19 as the last day to register before the November 3 General Election. The Department of State registration page confirms the 15-day rule.

polling_place.label: Find a Polling Place
polling_place.content: Use Pennsylvania's official polling-place lookup to find the Election Day polling place assigned to your residential address. Pennsylvania voters generally must go to the correct assigned polling place to cast a regular Election Day ballot. A voter who believes they are eligible to vote at a location but whose eligibility cannot be confirmed may request a provisional ballot. Polling locations can change, so voters should verify their location shortly before Election Day.
polling_place.source_name: Commonwealth of Pennsylvania — Find Your Local Polling Place
polling_place.internal_note: Pennsylvania's current polling-place guidance explicitly states that a voter at the wrong polling place must generally go to the correct location. A provisional ballot may be available when the voter believes they are eligible at the location. Reverify polling locations near Election Day.

election_day.label: Election Day Voting
election_day.content: Pennsylvania's General Election is Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Polling places are open from 7:00 a.m. until 8:00 p.m. A voter who is in line at or before 8:00 p.m. must be allowed to vote. Pennsylvania does not generally require identification every time a voter casts an in-person ballot. Identification is required when a voter appears to vote at a particular polling place for the first time. A voter who requested a mail ballot but did not return it may vote a regular ballot by surrendering the unvoted mail ballot and outer return envelope at the polling place. If the voter cannot surrender those materials, the voter may cast a provisional ballot.
election_day.source_name: Commonwealth of Pennsylvania — Find Your Local Polling Place
election_day.internal_note: The Department of State directly confirms 7:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. statewide polling hours and protects voters in line by 8:00 p.m. Pennsylvania does not have a universal in-person photo-ID requirement. The first-time-at-a-polling-place ID rule accepts both photo and qualifying non-photo identification. The Department also directly explains the surrender/provisional procedures for voters who requested mail ballots.

polling_hours.label: Polling Hours
polling_hours.content: Pennsylvania polling places are open from 7:00 a.m. until 8:00 p.m. on Election Day. Anyone who is in line at or before 8:00 p.m. must be allowed to cast a ballot.
polling_hours.source_name: Pennsylvania Department of State — Upcoming Elections
polling_hours.internal_note: Pennsylvania uses uniform statewide Election Day polling hours of 7:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. The Department's First Time Voters guidance directly confirms that voters in line by closing are permitted to vote.

early_voting.label: Voting Before Election Day
early_voting.content: Pennsylvania does not provide traditional in-person early voting at polling places. Instead, once a county's mail ballots are finalized and available, a registered voter may go to the county election office or another officially designated location, apply for a mail-in or absentee ballot, receive the ballot, complete it and return it during the same visit. This option is sometimes called on-demand mail ballot voting. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, the deadline to apply for a mail ballot through this process is 5:00 p.m. October 27. Availability before that date depends on when each county's ballots are finalized and ready.
early_voting.glance_value: On-demand mail ballot voting available; no traditional early polling
early_voting.source_name: Pennsylvania Department of State — On-Demand Mail Ballot Voting
early_voting.internal_note: This distinction is important. The Pennsylvania Department of State explicitly states that Pennsylvania does not have early voting in the way many states do. Voters can vote before Election Day only through the mail-ballot process. There are no ordinary polling places open for early voting. County availability begins when finalized ballots are ready, so no uniform statewide start date should be invented.

absentee_mail.label: Mail-in & Absentee Voting
absentee_mail.content: Pennsylvania offers two types of civilian mail ballots. Any registered voter may apply for a no-excuse mail-in ballot. Absentee ballots are available to registered voters who qualify because they cannot go to their polling place on Election Day for reasons such as illness, disability, work or travel. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, the county election office must receive an application for either type of ballot by 5:00 p.m. October 27. The county election office must receive the completed civilian mail ballot by 8:00 p.m. on November 3. An Election Day postmark is not sufficient. The voter must place the completed ballot in the official secrecy envelope, place that envelope inside the outer return envelope, and sign and write the current date on the voter's declaration as instructed. Voters generally must return their own mail ballots, with limited exceptions such as a voter with a disability who properly designates another person in writing.
absentee_mail.glance_value: No-excuse mail ballot; apply by 5:00 p.m. October 27
absentee_mail.source_name: Pennsylvania Department of State — Mail-in and Absentee Ballot
absentee_mail.internal_note: The current Department of State page directly establishes October 27 at 5:00 p.m. as the application deadline and November 3 at 8:00 p.m. as the receipt deadline. Pennsylvania has no postmark grace period for ordinary civilian mail ballots. Current state guidance also requires use of the yellow secrecy envelope and completion of the declaration on the outer return envelope. Emergency absentee procedures may be available after October 27 in qualifying circumstances.

voter_id.label: Voter ID Requirements
voter_id.content: Pennsylvania does not generally require voters to show identification every time they vote in person. A voter must show identification the first time the voter appears to vote at a particular polling place. Accepted photo identification includes a Pennsylvania driver's license or PennDOT identification card, identification issued by Pennsylvania or the U.S. government, a U.S. passport, U.S. Armed Forces identification, student identification and employee identification. Qualifying non-photo identification showing the voter's name and address may also be used, including a county voter registration card, government-issued non-photo identification, firearm permit, current utility bill, current bank statement, paycheck or government check. Mail-ballot applicants are subject to separate identification requirements.
voter_id.glance_value: ID required only the first time voting at a polling place
voter_id.source_name: Pennsylvania Department of State — First Time Voters
voter_id.internal_note: Pennsylvania should NOT be characterized as a general photo-ID state. The in-person requirement applies the first time a voter appears at a particular election district/polling place and permits both photo and specified non-photo identification. Mail voting has a separate identification process: applicants generally provide a Pennsylvania driver license/PennDOT ID number, last four digits of SSN or qualifying alternative documentation. UOCAVA and certain alternative-ballot voters are exempt from the ordinary mail-ballot ID requirement.

accessible_voting.label: Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.content: Every Pennsylvania polling place must provide at least one accessible voting system. Voters with disabilities may receive assistance and may generally choose a person to help them vote, subject to restrictions on certain people such as the voter's employer, union representative or Judge of Elections. Pennsylvania also provides an accessible remote ballot-marking solution that allows registered voters with disabilities who qualify for a mail-in or absentee ballot to access and mark the ballot electronically using screen readers or other assistive technology. The completed accessible mail ballot must still be returned to the county election office and received by the applicable deadline.
accessible_voting.glance_value: Accessible voting systems and remote ballot marking available
accessible_voting.source_name: Pennsylvania Department of State — Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.internal_note: The Department directly states that every polling place must have at least one accessible voting system. It also provides alternative ballots for qualifying voters age 65 or older or voters with disabilities assigned to inaccessible polling places. The accessible remote ballot-marking system permits electronic access and marking but requires the ballot to be returned under the mail-ballot procedures; it is not unrestricted online voting.

military_overseas.label: Military & Overseas Voting
military_overseas.content: Pennsylvania provides special registration and absentee-voting procedures for eligible uniformed-service members, qualifying family members and U.S. citizens living overseas. Covered voters may use the Federal Post Card Application to register and request an absentee ballot and may use the Federal Write-In Absentee Ballot when applicable. Military and civilian overseas voters may request electronic delivery of their absentee ballot. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, qualifying military and overseas absentee ballots must be submitted for delivery no later than 11:59 p.m. November 2 and received by the county election office no later than 5:00 p.m. November 10. Different rules apply to certain federal voters living overseas, whose ballots must be received by 8:00 p.m. on Election Day.
military_overseas.glance_value: FPCA and electronic ballot delivery available
military_overseas.source_name: Pennsylvania Department of State — Military and Overseas Voters
military_overseas.internal_note: The official 2026 election calendar establishes November 10 as the final receipt date for qualifying military and overseas absentee ballots submitted for delivery by 11:59 p.m. November 2. The Department distinguishes military voters, overseas civilian voters who intend to return to Pennsylvania, and federal voters living overseas who no longer maintain Pennsylvania residency. Federal voters may vote only for federal offices and have an 8:00 p.m. Election Day receipt deadline. Do not apply the seven-day UOCAVA receipt extension indiscriminately to every overseas category.

student_voting.label: College / Student Voting
student_voting.content: College students may register in Pennsylvania if they meet the state's eligibility and residency requirements. A student must be a U.S. citizen, be at least 18 years old on Election Day and have lived in the Pennsylvania election district where the student intends to vote for at least 30 days before the election. Students may use a qualifying campus residence as their voting address or may retain another qualifying voting residence, but may vote from only one residence in an election. Any registered Pennsylvania voter, including a college student, may request a no-excuse mail-in ballot. A student who votes for the first time at a particular Pennsylvania polling place must satisfy the state's first-time voter identification requirement; an accepted student identification, including an electronic or digital student ID card, may qualify.
student_voting.glance_value: Students may use a qualifying campus residence and no-excuse mail voting
student_voting.source_name: Pennsylvania Department of State — College Students
student_voting.internal_note: The Department's college-student guidance directly confirms the 30-day district residency requirement and no-excuse mail voting. Pennsylvania accepts student identification, including electronic/digital student ID, for the first-time-at-a-polling-place ID requirement when it meets the state's requirements. A student who moved to Pennsylvania fewer than 30 days before the election cannot register for that Pennsylvania election.

sample_ballot.label: Official Sample Ballot
sample_ballot.content: Pennsylvania sample ballots are provided through county election offices because ballot contents vary by election district and local contests. Voters can use the state's official polling-place and county-election resources to identify their county and election district, then review the sample ballot published by their county when it becomes available. Voters should check again close to the November 3, 2026 General Election after ballots have been finalized.
sample_ballot.glance_value: Check your county election office for your sample ballot
sample_ballot.source_name: Pennsylvania Department of State — County Election Officials
sample_ballot.internal_note: The Department's First Time Voters guidance specifically tells voters that sample ballots can be found on county election office websites. Pennsylvania's 67 county boards administer elections, and ballot contents vary locally. There is not one statewide sample ballot applicable to every voter.

contact.label: Contact the State Election Authority
contact.content: Pennsylvania Department of State voter and election assistance is available through the year-round election hotline at 1-877-VOTESPA (1-877-868-3772). Email: ra-voterreg@pa.gov. Interpretation services are available through the hotline. Pennsylvania's 67 county boards of elections administer elections locally, so voters should contact their county election office for voter-specific questions about registration, polling locations, mail ballots and local election procedures.
contact.source_name: Pennsylvania Department of State — Contact Us
contact.internal_note: The Department's current contact page verifies 1-877-868-3772 and [ra-voterreg@pa.gov](mailto:ra-voterreg@pa.gov). Pennsylvania elections are administered by 67 county boards of elections. The email address is intentionally plain text with no Markdown or mailto wrapper.

official_resources.label: Official State & Local Resources
official_resources.content: Use the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania's official Voting and Election Information resources for statewide voter information. These resources provide voter registration, registration status, polling-place lookup, mail-in and absentee voting, accessible voting, military and overseas voting, election dates and county election office contacts. Pennsylvania's 67 county boards of elections administer polling places, voter records, mail ballots and other local election functions.
official_resources.glance_value: Pennsylvania Department of State & 67 county election boards
